clue.text: Large sum advanced, except for bank vault content?

parts.note: G is short for grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
advanced in years means old
bar is a preposition meaning except for

explanation.surface: A financier talks about a big sum being lent, with one exception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Large sum advanced' reads as a loan, but splits into G (grand) and OLD (advanced in age).
explanation.definitionFit: Bullion ingots are the classic treasure stacked inside a bank's strongroom; the question mark flags the example.

clue.text: Cut by aluminium — blood everywhere

indicators.note: the word for blood is cut open with the metal's symbol placed in it

parts.note: gore is spilt blood
Al is the chemical symbol for aluminium

explanation.surface: A grisly scene: someone sliced by a metal blade, blood all over.
explanation.definitionFit: Something found in abundance, in great plenty, can loosely be said to be all over the place.

clue.text: Peanuts stand stars

parts.note: peanuts is slang for a trifling amount, very little
to stand something is to bear or tolerate it

explanation.surface: Characters from the Peanuts comic strip appear on a stand of celebrities.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peanuts' looks like the Charlie Brown strip, and 'stars' like celebrities; here they are a small sum and a constellation.
explanation.definitionFit: Ursa Minor, the small constellation holding the Pole Star, is a group of stars.

clue.text: "Working as fast as possible" at the heart of perverse "British complaint"

indicators.note: the two short pieces sit in the middle of the jumbled word
perverse means contrary or twisted, so the letters of British are rearranged

parts.note: on means operating or working
c, the speed of light, is the fastest anything can go

explanation.surface: A grumble about a working culture that demands maximum speed, called a typically British complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perverse' scrambles the letters of British, and 'at the heart of' puts the two short pieces inside. C as the speed of light is a physics convention. 'British complaint' looks like one phrase but only 'complaint' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaint here means an ailment; inflammation of the airways is a medical complaint.

clue.text: Crafty makeover, note, to get really attractive

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
fit is British slang for sexy or very attractive

explanation.surface: A craft-project makeover leaves a note on how gorgeous the result looks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crafty' suggests arts and crafts or cunning, but means relating to a craft, a ship. FIT as 'attractive' is British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship or boat (a craft) that is overhauled and re-equipped gets a renovation in the dockyard.

clue.text: Tasteless entrances by one backward duck

parts.note: ins are ways in, entrances
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: backward tells us the word for duck runs from right to left

parts.note: to duck is to dip under

explanation.surface: A dull doorway beside a waddling duck.
explanation.definitionFit: Insipid food lacks flavour, so it is without taste.

clue.text: Telling off about orange tank tops wrongly taken

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the jumbled letters go round the two initials
off means awry or wrong, so the letters of Telling are rearranged
tops means the first letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Someone is scolded over an orange tank top acquired dishonestly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges TELLING into ILLG...TEN, which goes 'about' OT, the 'tops' of orange and tank.
explanation.definitionFit: Gains acquired by dishonest or unlawful means are obtained improperly.

clue.text: A comedy classic — but not 13 as far as 7 is concerned

definitions.meaning: the 1959 Billy Wilder film with Marilyn Monroe and Jack Lemmon

definitions.text: not 13 as far as 7 is concerned
definitions.meaning: in the fairy tale, Goldilocks (13) chose the porridge (7) that was neither too hot nor too cold, so she was not one of those who preferred it scalding

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-references to 13 (GOLDILOCKS) and 7 (PORRIDGE) point to the fairy tale of Goldilocks and the three bears.
explanation.definitionFit: The film title is a famous screen comedy, and read literally it says certain people prefer things scalding.

clue.text: Breakfast TV series?

definitions.meaning: a morning meal of oats cooked in milk or water
the 1970s BBC sitcom starring Ronnie Barker as a prisoner; the title is also slang for a prison sentence

explanation.walkthrough: 'Breakfast TV' looks like morning television, but splits into two separate definitions.
explanation.definitionFit: Oat gruel is a breakfast staple, and the same title belongs to a classic British prison comedy.

clue.text: Separate, hellish destination holiday island

parts.note: Dis is the classical underworld, the city of hell in Dante
Crete is a Greek island popular with holidaymakers

explanation.surface: A holiday island described as a nightmare destination best kept apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinct and individually distinguishable things are kept apart from each other.

clue.text: Bishop withdraws from loaded numbers game

indicators.note: withdraws from means the bishop's letter leaves the word for loaded

parts.note: loaded and blotto are both slang for very drunk
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A cleric pulls out of a rigged gambling game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loaded' suggests weighted dice or wealth, but means drunk, BLOTTO.
explanation.definitionFit: A lottery-style game where players match drawn numbers is a game of numbers.

clue.text: Satisfied with comedy brothers broadcast, all the boxes being ticked?

parts.note: full means satisfied after eating

indicators.note: broadcast means the brothers' surname is heard spoken rather than written

parts.note: the Marx Brothers were the American comedy team of Groucho, Harpo and Chico

explanation.surface: A contented viewer of a Marx Brothers film on air, everything checked off.
explanation.definitionFit: A perfect score in a test means every answer was right and earned a tick.

clue.text: Moving elsewhere, rejected old king breaks into allowance

indicators.note: the reversed king pushes inside the word for allowance

parts.note: a ration is a fixed allowance

indicators.note: rejected means turned back, so the king's name is read backwards

parts.note: Old King Cole is the merry old soul of the nursery rhyme

explanation.surface: An exiled former monarch forces his way into the stores while moving house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' turns the king's name backwards (Old King Cole of the nursery rhyme) and 'breaks into' puts it just after the first letter of the allowance.
explanation.definitionFit: A move to a new place, home or office, is a change of location.

clue.text: Stout-sounding person's last stand?

indicators.note: sounding means the word for stout is heard, then spelt differently

parts.note: stout is a dark beer

explanation.surface: A sturdy-looking person making a final heroic defence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stout' looks like an adjective for the person, but is the dark drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A coffin rests on this frame before burial, so it is the final platform anyone stands on, jokingly.

clue.text: Old Nick ogles Oz for moulding into Earth's ideal location

indicators.note: moulding means reshaping, so the letters of the four words are rearranged

explanation.surface: The Devil eyes up Australia as the perfect spot to reshape into his own world.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Nick' is the Devil and 'Oz' Australia, but here they are only letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomers name the habitable band around a star, neither too hot nor too cold, after the fairy tale; our planet sits in it.

clue.text: 1,000 quickly pocketed in criminal delight — fancy!

indicators.note: pocketed in means held inside the rearranged letters
criminal means wrong or bad, so the letters of delight are rearranged

parts.note: thou is informal shorthand for a thousand, the quick way of saying it

explanation.surface: A thief gleefully pockets a grand in a flash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges DELIGHT into IDLE...GHT, holding THOU.
explanation.definitionFit: A fancy, as a noun, is an imagined notion or whim, an idle musing.

clue.text: See 6
Was the leader — having gagged Brown — made to take responsibility?

indicators.note: gagging puts something in a mouth, so the colour goes inside

parts.note: led means was at the front or in charge
umber is a brown earth pigment

explanation.surface: A leader who silenced Gordon Brown is then forced to carry the blame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brown' looks like a politician's surname, but is the colour, UMBER.
explanation.definitionFit: To be saddled or burdened with an unwanted duty is the British sense of the word.

clue.text: Appear to favour both sides of violin (one taken from Glen)

parts.note: Strad is short for a Stradivarius violin

indicators.note: taken from means one letter is removed from the valley word

parts.note: a dale is a valley, like a glen
a means one

explanation.surface: A violinist from Glen seems to back both factions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Glen' looks like a person's name, but is a valley, DALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who sits on the fence, taking a position across an issue, seems to back both camps.

clue.text: Managed kitchen in nude — daft as clear soup!

indicators.note: in means the rearranged kitchen sits inside the other jumbled word
daft means silly, so the letters of nude are rearranged
managed means handled or worked, so the letters of kitchen are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone ran a kitchen naked, which was as daft as a clear soup is thin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Managed' turns KITCHEN into THICKEN, sitting 'in' UN...ED, the 'daft' anagram of NUDE.
explanation.definitionFit: A consommé is a thin broth that has not been given body with flour or cream.

clue.text: Medium infiltrates bizarre adult religious authority

indicators.note: infiltrates means the size letter slips inside the jumbled word
bizarre means odd, so the letters of adult are rearranged

parts.note: M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium

explanation.surface: A psychic sneaks into a strange grown-up's religious circle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Medium' suggests a psychic, but gives the size M.
explanation.definitionFit: The body of Jewish civil and ceremonial law is a source of rabbinic guidance.

clue.text: Bush, being well on right, let off

parts.note: my is an exclamation of surprise, like well!

indicators.note: off means wrong or awry, so the letters of let are rearranged

explanation.surface: George Bush, doing well with the political right, is excused.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bush' looks like the president, but is a shrub.
explanation.definitionFit: An evergreen shrub with fragrant white flowers is a kind of shrub.

clue.text: See 2
Variety broadcast: "Miss Fitzgerald at New York"

indicators.note: broadcast means the phrase is heard spoken aloud

parts.note: Miss Ella (Fitzgerald, the jazz singer) plus NY for New York

explanation.surface: A radio variety show announces Ella Fitzgerald performing in New York.
explanation.definitionFit: A mixed collection of assorted items is a medley of many kinds.

clue.text: I say restricting crossword setters is to display fear!

indicators.note: restricting means holding in, so the exclamation goes round the pronoun

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like I say
setters refer to themselves as we, or the setter collectively

explanation.surface: An exclaimed claim that boxing in puzzle compilers makes them tremble.
explanation.definitionFit: To shrink back or crouch in terror is to show fright.

clue.text: See 13
Receivers question broadcast entertainment

parts.note: radios are receiving sets
how is a question word

explanation.surface: Someone asks about the sets that pick up programmes.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme on the wireless is entertainment that goes out over the airwaves.

clue.text: Member of rock band that blazed a trail?

definitions.meaning: one of the ..., Bill Haley's rock and roll band
a celestial body of ice and dust that leaves a glowing tail across the sky

explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock band' points to Bill Haley and His Comets; 'blazed a trail' is literal for the celestial body.
explanation.definitionFit: A Haley bandsman was one of the Comets, and the heavenly body streaks a bright tail through space.

clue.text: Right way to secure Guardian's precise direction

parts.note: due is what one has a right to
the Guardian newspaper speaks of itself as we
St is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: The newspaper declares its exact correct course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Right way' looks like the definition but is two pieces; 'to secure' has the street abbreviation hold the paper's editorial pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Heading exactly towards the sunset, with no deviation, is an exact compass bearing.

clue.text: Remains of small house one expected

parts.note: res is short for residence, a house
I is the Roman numeral one
due means expected, as a baby or train is due

explanation.surface: What's left of a little home someone was waiting for.
explanation.definitionFit: Whatever is left over after the rest has gone is the leftover portion.
